STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of steamed broccoli florets on a white square plate, photographed from above (near top-down angle).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 22 cm across (its width spans most of the frame height, about 24 cm at the outer rim). Using an effective diameter of ~22 cm: area = 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Broccoli florets (about 6 pieces, cooked, bright green). No visible sauce or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: Florets cover roughly 30% of the plate area (about 115 cm^2), concentrated in the center.

STEP 5 - Volume: Average pile height about 3 cm for the florets, giving a gross volume of about 115 x 3 ≈ 345 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetables at 0.5-0.7 g/ml; use 0.55 for loose florets with gaps. 345 x 0.55 ≈ 190 g. (Florets are fairly airy, so this is a reasonable upper-middle estimate.)

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked broccoli is about 35 kcal per 100 g. 190 g x 0.35 ≈ 67 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Six florets totaling about 190 g is plausible for a side portion (roughly 1.5 cups of cooked broccoli would be ~150 g). Total around 190 g and 65-70 kcal fits what is visible.

Summary: about 190 g of steamed broccoli, about 67 kcal.
